result:
**I would make every human being genuinely curious about the perspectives, lived experiences, and inner worlds of people who are different from them.**

Not tolerance. Not "empathy" as a buzzword. Real, burning curiosity.

If that single switch flipped in humanity tomorrow, almost every major problem we face would start solving itself over time:

- Polarization would collapse because people would actually want to understand why someone thinks differently instead of scoring points.
- Prejudice would wither because curiosity is incompatible with lazy stereotypes.
- Wars and systemic cruelty would become much harder to sustain when enough people are compelled to truly see the humanity on the other side.
- Loneliness would decrease because curiosity naturally builds connection.
- Even environmental destruction and short-term thinking would face pressure, because curious people tend to think in systems and long time horizons.

Curiosity is the one trait that reliably leads to humility, learning, compassion, and creativity all at once. It's the ultimate antidote to both ignorance and arrogance.

Everything else (better technology, better systems, better laws) eventually gets corrupted or gamed by humans who aren't curious about the experiences of the people those systems affect. But if you fix the curiosity problem, the rest becomes solvable.

So yeah. One change.

Make us all insatiably, uncomfortably, wonderfully curious about each other. The rest would follow.
